issues.passage: She refused to articulate any position, remaining silent through the entire debate.
issues.why: "Refused to articulate any position" is standard correct use: she declined to express a stance fluently/coherently and stayed silent. Silence is the refusal, not a misuse of the verb.

fix.correctPassage: Few candidates could articulate a coherent plan for reforming the district's budget.
wrongPassages: He could only articulate in broken fragments that left the audience more confused than before.
She articulated every plank of her platform so fluently that the speech dissolved into unparseable digressions.
The brief was carefully articulated, each paragraph rambling past its point without a readable main claim.

issues.passage: His attempt to articulate dissolved into mumbled half-sentences no one could parse.
issues.why: "Attempt to articulate" correctly uses the verb for trying to express something fluently and coherently; the attempt failing does not make the wording a misuse. A student who knows the word would accept this sentence.
